claims.text: The ball-milled Mg-Al-Ti-V-Fe-Co powder is a BCC solid solution.
Mechanical alloying leaves residual oxygen and a high density of defects in the powder.
Mg-Al-Ti-V-Fe-Co can be consolidated by SPS at 950 °C, 30–50 MPa, and a 10–20 minute hold under vacuum or argon.
Sintering at 950 °C precipitates a nanoscale, continuous (Al,Ti)-rich BCC intermetallic network at grain boundaries and triple junctions.
High configurational entropy initially stabilizes the BCC solid solution in Mg-Al-Ti-V-Fe-Co.
At 950 °C, increased diffusion enables Al and Ti to segregate and nucleate secondary BCC phases.
Al and Ti have sufficiently negative mixing enthalpies and large atomic radii to drive the proposed segregation and precipitation.
Atomic-size mismatch and mixing-enthalpy differences cause specific (Al,Ti)-rich precipitation rather than random segregation.
The continuous precipitate network impedes long-range Mg diffusion and thereby suppresses Mg volatilization.
The continuous precipitate network impedes oxygen diffusion and suppresses bulk oxidation.
The precipitates pin grain boundaries, refine the grain size, and increase hardness through Hall–Petch strengthening.
A sample sintered at 950 °C will attain more than 95% theoretical density.
A sample sintered at 950 °C will have more than 30% greater Vickers hardness than material treated below 800 °C.
A sample sintered at 950 °C will exhibit two- to threefold lower oxidation weight gain than samples sintered at 800 °C or 1050 °C.
At 800 °C, insufficient driving force produces low density and prevents secondary-phase precipitation.
Above 1000 °C, Mg vapor pressure causes rapid Mg loss and composition deviation.
Mg loss above 1000 °C disrupts the protective intermetallic network, increases porosity, and reduces corrosion resistance.
Oxygen introduced during milling may form oxides that compete with formation of the desired intermetallic barrier.
A continuous (Al,Ti)-rich grain-boundary structure should correlate with a thinner oxide scale and lower oxidation weight gain.
Oxidation weight-gain curves and post-mortem oxide/interface analyses can distinguish the proposed diffusion-barrier mechanism from alternative oxidation behavior.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome and boundary imply that the 1050 °C sample should oxidize more and have poorer protection than the 950 °C sample. The falsification rule nevertheless says that a thicker oxide scale at 1050 °C would invalidate the boundary. A thicker scale would ordinarily be consistent with, rather than contrary to, the claimed loss of protection. The rule also conflates a thicker scale with a more protective scale.
The material contains six metallic elements, but the uncertainty field calls Mg-Al-Ti-V-Fe-Co a quinary system.
